text:
maya: :rotating_light: noticing 5xx spike from eu-west-1 customers — multiple reports of model API 503s. traceroutes show some traffic to a dark IP in the wrong AZ. Can oncall take?
incident-bot: Pager sent to @devops-oncall — priority: P1 — runbook: network-outage -> paging.ack required.
liam (oncall): acked. rolling in. quick ask: any recent infra changes in eu-west-1?
maya: we pushed a small route-table update 40m ago for burst subnets (terraform apply by infra-deploy).
liam (oncall): copy. can someone paste recent route-table/NGW changes?
cheng (support): customers affected: 3 mid-market accounts with high-volume inference jobs, UX errors start at ~12:18UTC. No data leakage reports, just failed connections and increased latency before 5xx.
liam (oncall): running checks: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcde --region eu-west-1`
dev-infra-bot: route-table rtb-0f3a returned. Attached to subnet-0a, subnet-0b. Routes: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0deadbeef, local routes OK.
liam (oncall): checking NAT health: `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --nat-gateway-ids nat-0deadbeef --region eu-west-1`
dev-infra-bot: nat-0deadbeef state: available, but metrics show high packet drops and >50% error rate at 12:17-12:25UTC.
liam (oncall): hm. timeout window matches customer reports. also checking DNS: doing dig for model-host.prod.redwood.net from within an affected pod:```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> model-host.prod.redwood.net +short
10.12.34.56
```
liam (oncall): that IP is in eu-north-1 IP range. shouldn't be. split-horizon DNS? Were any Route53 entries updated?
maya: we updated a private hosted zone A-records for some canary hosts earlier, but not the public prod zone. I didn't touch model-host.
liam (oncall): running Route53 query for prod zone: `aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --query "ResourceRecordSets[?Name=='model-host.prod.redwood.net.']"`
dev-infra-bot: record-set shows A -> 10.12.34.56 with TTL 300. Change history: modified 12:15UTC by infra-deploy user.
liam (oncall): ok here's the story so far: route-table change earlier plus a Route53 update simultaneously. Combined they created a split where DNS resolves to an IP in eu-north-1 but that IP's NAT/route config doesn't accept our traffic, producing 503s. Need to mitigate ASAP.
cheng (support): customer impact summary: ~25% of requests from eu-west-1 tenants get 503s, some automatic retries reduce effective throughput but batch jobs failing. SLA-blippable for one account — prepping incident email.
liam (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) revert Route53 change to previous A record (roll back via change batch) 2) if traffic still broken, failover to secondary NAT in eu-west-1 (create replacement NAT and update route) 3) reduce TTL to 60 during flip and then raise. I'll attempt 1 now.
maya: I'm with you for rollback. infra-deploy creds standing by.
liam (oncall): executing Route53 rollback:```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"model-host.prod.redwood.net.","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.65.23.11"}]}}]}'```
dev-infra-bot: change submitted. change-id C0ABC submitted at 12:28UTC. status: PENDING.
liam (oncall): waiting for change to propagate. tailing logs.
cheng (support): alerted impacted customers, included mitigation steps and ETA ~10-15m.
liam (oncall): Route53 change now INSYNC. doing curl from app pod to model-host.prod.redwood.net -> 52.65.23.11. Getting 200s now. :thumbsup:
maya: monitoring metrics — error rate falling from 25% to 2% over last 4 minutes. latency normalizing.
liam (oncall): still going to create a replacement NAT to be safe — provisioning now: `aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-0a --allocation-id eipalloc-0bcd --region eu-west-1`
dev-infra-bot: nat-0cafe state: pending at 12:36UTC -> available at 12:42UTC.
liam (oncall): updating route table to point 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0cafe for the affected subnets. done.
maya: confirmed data plane back to eu-west-1 NAT. metrics green.
liam (oncall): root cause (prelim): concurrent infra changes — a stale change to public host A records pointed prod name to an IP not owned by eu-west-1, combined with a prior route update created transient path mismatches. We'll do RCA after stabilization.
sophia (next-oncall): wrapping handoff. I'm taking this for post-incident checks and RCA. summary: reverted Route53, provisioned replacement NAT, updated route tables, customers recovering. I'll coordinate RCA and postmortem doc.
cheng (support): prepping post-incident customer notes and credit calculations. will attach affected request ids and timelines.
liam (oncall): handing off full logs to @sophia. key artifacts: Route53 change-id C0ABC, NAT metrics, route-table diffs (terraform plan output).
maya: will open a git issue linking infra change request and the quick rollback performed.
sophia (next-oncall): thanks — will run config drift checks and verify no other hosted zones were changed. Also we'll add an extra guard in the deploy pipeline to warn on simultaneous DNS+network ops.
liam (oncall): closing active pager. leaving incident thread open for RCA. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)
incident-bot: Incident P1 marked resolved at 12:45UTC. Playbook: network-outage -> follow-up required.
cheng (support): final customer impact note: three accounts affected for ~27 mins peak, transient job failures mostly recovered. draft email ready.
sophia (next-oncall): scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow 09:00UTC. will include infra, devexp, and support.
maya: thanks everyone.
